metadata.note: The First Transcontinental Railroad: a 1,911-mile continuous line completed May 10 1869 when the Central Pacific Railroad (built east from Sacramento) met the Union Pacific Railroad (built west from Council Bluffs/Omaha) at Promontory Summit, Utah, marked by the ceremonial Golden Spike. This is modeled as two features -- Union Pacific and Central Pacific -- meeting at Promontory Summit. Southern Pacific's Lucin Cutoff (completed 1904) later bypassed this original route around the north end of the Great Salt Lake with a more direct trestle crossing, relegating the Corinne-Lucin segment through Promontory Summit to secondary/local status; that original segment was fully abandoned in 1942, its rails scrapped for the WWII war effort. Both features therefore end in 1942 -- Promontory Summit today is a National Historic Site with no active track, and modern Amtrak/UP/SP-successor traffic instead runs via the Lucin Cutoff and other realignments further south (compare against amtrak.geojson's California Zephyr routing). Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation based on documented end-of-track/station towns, straight-line segments between them -- NOT digitized from period track maps, so curvature within each town-to-town segment is schematic rather than surveyed. REFINEMENT (2026-08-18): the Nebraska portion originally jumped straight from Fremont to North Platte in one ~360km line, skipping the Platte Valley towns the railroad was actually built through. It now follows Columbus, Central City, Grand Island, Wood River, Kearney, Lexington, Cozad (the 100th Meridian marker) and Gothenburg, matching the documented 1865-66 construction sequence. Still hand-placed town waypoints, not surveyed track centerline. FURTHER REFINEMENT (2026-08-22): densified the Wyoming/Utah portion of the UP segment (Cheyenne to Ogden) with Sherman Summit (8,204ft, the original line's highest point, reached ~April 1868), Benton (a 'Hell on Wheels' end-of-track town near the North Platte River crossing, summer 1868), Rock Springs (coal town reached 1868), Bryan (Sept 1868, briefly the end-of-track terminus near Green River), and Wahsatch (where UP crews entered Utah Territory at the head of Echo Canyon, late Dec 1868). Also densified the Central Pacific segment with Newcastle and Cisco, CA (1865-66, on the Sierra Nevada crossing between Sacramento and Truckee) and Terrace and Kelton, UT (CP section/maintenance stations built into the Great Salt Lake Desert in 1869, between Wells, NV and Promontory). Coordinates for the smaller ghost-town sites (Benton, Bryan, Wahsatch, Terrace, Kelton) are approximate placements based on descriptive historical sources, not surveyed positions. REAL TRACE (2026-08-26): the town-waypoint approximation described above has been replaced. Both features are now traced from OpenStreetMap way geometry by corridor-constrained shortest path - 2,315 points over 1,043.3 mi for the Union Pacific half and 2,788 points over 681.9 mi for the Central Pacific half, against documented mileages of 1,086 and 690, with no straight-line connectors on the UP half and a single 22 m connector on the CP half. Where the 1869 alignment was abandoned and is still mapped in OSM the trace follows the ORIGINAL grade rather than the modern main line: the 1868 Sherman Summit / Dale Creek line between Buford and Laramie WY, the 1868 Donner Pass line through Summit Tunnel #6 and Tunnel #8, and the whole Corinne-Promontory-Lucin grade abandoned in 1942. Where it was not - most notably Aspen Ridge WY, where the trace runs on the post-1901 Aspen Tunnel alignment - the drawn line is a LATER alignment than the feature's own era; each feature's geometry_quality field names every such stretch, and also lists the places where OSM maps the track so coarsely that consecutive nodes are kilometres apart.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact 1869-era station stop list and mileage beyond the well-documented end-of-track towns; precise frequency/timetable for either era (1869-1904 mainline vs. 1904-1942 secondary status), both estimated; the Central Pacific's eastern extension to Oakland/San Francisco Bay (Western Pacific Railroad segment, also completed 1869) is not modeled here as a separate feature.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap way geometry (ODbL), fetched 2026-08-26 via Overpass in 28 bbox tiles covering the corridor, assembled by corridor-constrained Dijkstra over the OSM node graph and simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 5 m. Route validated by checking the traced line passes within 1 km of every geocoded 1869 station town used to build the corridor (Sherman Summit is the one deliberate 4 km exception - the trace follows the original 1868 grade there, the geocoded reference is the modern line).

segments.note: Union Pacific construction west from Omaha up the Platte River valley - the same corridor wagon trains had followed since the 1840s - reached Fremont Dec 31 1865, Columbus Jun 2 1866, Grand Island Jul 8 1866, Kearney by Aug 1866 (a correspondent called it 'small, but vigorous and promising'), the 100th Meridian just west of today's Cozad on Oct 5 1866 (marked with a sign reading '100th MERIDIAN. 247 MILES FROM OMAHA'), and North Platte in late 1866. UP mainline segment of the First Transcontinental Railroad, completed 1869; frequency estimated/unsourced

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap way geometry (2026-08-26), not hand-placed waypoints: a corridor-constrained shortest path over every OSM railway way within 25 km of a corridor built from 61 geocoded 1869 station towns (Council Bluffs - Omaha - Fremont - Columbus - Grand Island - Kearney - North Platte - Ogallala - Julesburg - Sidney - Pine Bluffs - Cheyenne - Buford - Laramie - Medicine Bow - Rawlins - Wamsutter - Point of Rocks - Rock Springs - Green River - Granger - Carter - Piedmont - Evanston - Wahsatch - Echo - Henefer - Morgan - Ogden - Brigham City - Corinne - Promontory). TRACED LENGTH 1,043.4 mi against a documented 1,086 mi Omaha-Promontory - 96% of the documented mileage. Of that, 992.3 mi is on today's active Union Pacific main line and 51.1 mi is on abandoned grade. No straight-line connectors were used anywhere: every metre of the drawn line sits on a mapped OSM way. The ~43-mile shortfall against the documented figure is mostly OSM's own coarseness - 65 places where consecutive mapped nodes are more than 1.5 km apart, 77 mi in total, the longest a 4.0 km tangent near Table Rock WY and a 3.8 km tangent at Medicine Bow WY - plus a century and a half of curve-easing on the surviving main line. Those long chords cut whatever curvature the real track has between their endpoints. ERA CAVEATS - the drawn line is the 1869 alignment only where the 1869 alignment still exists on the ground: (a) Sherman Hill WY, Buford to Laramie, ~14 mi: drawn on the ORIGINAL 1868 grade over Sherman Summit including the Dale Creek crossing (OSM railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=UP), NOT the 1901 Hermosa realignment that carries today's trains, which lies up to ~4 km south of it. (b) Aspen Ridge WY, west of Carter toward Evanston: drawn on the POST-1901 Aspen Tunnel alignment. The original 1869 line over Aspen summit is essentially unmapped in OSM (about 1 km of grade survives in the data), so this stretch is a later alignment than the feature's own era, off its 1869 position by up to a few miles. (c) Corinne to Promontory UT: drawn on the abandoned original grade (railway=abandoned), which is correct for 1869 and is not the 1904 Lucin Cutoff. (d) Everywhere else the drawn line is today's UP main line. It occupies the 1869 corridor, but has been realigned in detail - curve easings, second-track construction, grade separations - repeatedly since, so it should be read as the corridor rather than as surveyed 1869 track centreline. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 9 ruled segments totalling 163 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: CP mainline segment of the First Transcontinental Railroad, completed 1869; frequency estimated/unsourced Wadsworth-Winnemucca detail per the CP's 1868 survey report and period travel accounts: from Wadsworth (Big Bend of the Truckee, reached July 22 1868) the line crossed ~40 miles of the Truckee-Humboldt Desert (Hot Springs, Mirage, White Plains) to the west side of Humboldt Lake, crossed the Humboldt River a few miles above the lake, then followed the river's east bank north through Lovelock's, Oreana, Rye Patch, and Mill City to Winnemucca (reached Sept 16 1868, first train Oct 1) - about 136 miles total. Crews laid a record 6 miles 200 feet of track in a single day near Humboldt City on Aug 19 1868, reflecting how much faster this flat desert/valley terrain was to build than the Sierra Nevada crossing.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap way geometry (2026-08-26), not hand-placed waypoints: a corridor-constrained shortest path over every OSM railway way within 25 km of a corridor built from 42 geocoded 1869 station towns (Sacramento - Roseville - Newcastle - Auburn - Colfax - Dutch Flat - Emigrant Gap - Cisco - Norden - Truckee - Verdi - Reno - Wadsworth - Lovelock - Rye Patch - Mill City - Winnemucca - Golconda - Battle Mountain - Beowawe - Carlin - Elko - Halleck - Deeth - Wells - Montello - Lucin - Terrace - Kelton - Promontory). TRACED LENGTH 682.1 mi against a documented 690 mi Sacramento-Promontory - 99% of the documented mileage. Of that, 578.9 mi is on today's active Union Pacific main line and 103.2 mi is on abandoned grade. One straight-line connector, 22 m long, was needed to bridge a break in the OSM ways; the rest of the line sits entirely on mapped OSM geometry. OSM's own coarseness is heavier on this half than on the UP's: 52 places where consecutive mapped nodes are more than 1.5 km apart, 85.7 mi in total, including a 9.5 km chord across the Carson Sink near Parran NV and a 9.2 km chord along the Humboldt between Golconda and Valmy NV. Those chords cut whatever curvature the real track has between their endpoints - the desert tangents genuinely are near-straight, but the Humboldt River stretches are not, and no better-mapped parallel way exists in OSM to route over instead. ERA CAVEATS - the drawn line is the 1869 alignment only where the 1869 alignment still exists on the ground: (a) Donner Pass CA, about 6 mi either side of the summit: drawn on the ORIGINAL 1868 line through Summit Tunnel #6 and Tunnel #8 (OSM railway=abandoned), NOT the 1925 Tunnel 41 'Big Hole' that carries today's trains. (b) Lucin to Promontory UT, ~97 mi: drawn on the abandoned original grade (railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=SP, including the named Central Pacific Railroad Grade (1869-1942), Old Railroad Grade and Big Fill ways), which is correct for 1869 and is not the 1904 Lucin Cutoff. (c) Sacramento to Wells NV: today's UP main line, occupying the 1869 corridor but realigned in detail many times since. (d) The drawn line passes about 1 mi from the geocoded Wadsworth NV townsite, the 1869 station at the Big Bend of the Truckee. Whether that offset is a later realignment of the main line or simply an artifact of comparing track to a town centroid has not been checked. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 5 ruled segments totalling 86 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).
